title: Private deployment: Granular egress proxy and offline orchestration acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This ticket defines requirements and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC deployments that must operate under strict egress constraints and in partially or fully air-gapped environments. The goal is to provide a repeatable operator contract for upgrades and runtime network fallbacks that preserves security posture while enabling safe, verifiable upgrades and observability.
requirements: Operators must be able to configure per-cluster granular egress allowlists and a single outbound proxy endpoint for all runtime control-plane traffic.
The platform must support both online upgrade flows (curl/HTTPS to Redwood mirrors) and offline artifact ingestion (signed tarball via operator media or OCI registry mirror).
All artifacts (images, charts, binaries) must be signed; the platform verifies signatures and checksums before applying upgrades.
Support mutual TLS (mTLS) for all control-plane egress to Redwood-managed endpoints or customer-managed mirrors, with configurable client cert rotation windows.

Provide an embargoed fallback mode: when egress to primary mirrors is unavailable, cluster can switch to a preconfigured local mirror or operator-provided artifact store with validated image provenance.
Upgrade orchestration must include staged canaries with configurable traffic percentages, health gating, and automatic rollback on defined failure signals.
Provide a deterministic simulation harness for network partitions (simulated blackholes, latency spikes, DNS failures) used in acceptance tests.
Observability hooks: expose upgrade progress metrics, artifact verification status, and egress connectivity checks to Prometheus endpoints and structured audit logs retained per org policy.
Document clearly the minimal network allowlist: destination IPs/CIDRs, DNS entries, ports, and protocols required for normal operation, canary upgrades, and emergency rollback.
Operator-facing CLI/Console must provide pre-upgrade validation checks and a dry-run mode that validates artifact signatures, mirror accessibility, and KMS connectivity (if applicable).
acceptance_criteria: Pre-upgrade validation: running 'redwoodctl preflight --cluster <id>' returns pass on artifact signature verification, mirror reachability, and KMS availability for online and offline modes.
Image provenance: When an upgrade is initiated with offline artifacts, the cluster verifies GPG/OCI signatures and rejects unsigned or tampered artifacts.
Egress config: Admins can define a single egress proxy FQDN and a per-cluster allowlist; the runtime rejects outbound connections outside allowlist when enforcement is enabled.
mTLS: Control-plane egress to mirrors succeeds using configured client certs; rotation triggers no more than 60s of degraded calls in automated tests.
Fallback behavior: If primary mirror is unreachable, cluster fails over to configured local mirror within the defined timeout and logs a categorized audit event.
Canary rollout: A 10% canary upgrade with health gating passes when healthy and is promoted to 100% automatically; if health checks fail, system rolls back to previous version within SLA window.
Partition simulation: Under simulated DNS failure to mirrors, the operator can perform an offline upgrade using a signed artifact; acceptance test completes without requiring external egress.
Observability: Upgrade progress, verification status, and egress failures are emitted to Prometheus with metric names and labels matching the observability spec and visible in the Console timeline.
Audit logging: Every upgrade event (start, artifact hash, canary promote/rollback) is logged with timestamp, actor, and result, and is downloadable from the Console for at least 90 days.
Documentation: Runbook for offline upgrades and emergency rollback is present in the Console help and linked from the preflight output.
Backward compatibility: Clusters running runtime-1.x must be able to validate signed artifacts produced by the current release artifact signing service.
tests: Automated preflight suite: validate artifact signature rejection and acceptance paths using both valid and intentionally corrupted artifacts.
mTLS rotation test: rotate client certs during an ongoing low-traffic period and measure service continuity and metrics for < 60s degradation.
Mirror failover test: block traffic to primary mirror IPs and verify automatic switch to local mirror and correct audit event generation.
Offline upgrade test: perform a full offline upgrade using operator-provided signed tarball delivered over removable media; verify successful startup and metrics emission.
Canary rollback test: introduce regression in canary, ensure automated health gate triggers rollback and cluster returns to previously known-good state within SLA.
Partition simulation harness: run chaos scenarios (latency, packet loss, DNS blackhole) and validate operator procedures from runbook can restore cluster without data loss.
End-to-end observability test: confirm Prometheus metrics, Console timeline, and audit logs contain consistent, correlated entries for the same upgrade event.
Pen test checklist: verify that egress allowlist cannot be bypassed by container escape or injected jobs; escalate findings if bypass exists.
dependencies: ENG-36210 (runtime artifact signature verification library updates)
ENG-39102 (mTLS client cert rotation support in control-plane agent)
PM-92734 (private deploy artifact distribution protocol spec)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Operators misconfigure mirror allowlists and accidentally block necessary egress. Mitigation: Provide conservative default allowlist templates and a preflight validator that simulates egress checks.
Risk: Offline upgrades may introduce operator errors when using removable media. Mitigation: Strict artifact signature checks, clear CLI prompts, and idempotent apply semantics to reduce human error.
Risk: Certificate rotation could cause brief outages. Mitigation: staggered rotation with overlap windows and automated retries with exponential backoff.
Risk: Observability blind spots during partitions. Mitigation: local buffering of audit events and a recovery sync job that reconciles events post-partition.
Risk: Regulatory constraints on audit retention. Mitigation: surface retention config in Console and provide export hooks for long-term archival.
operator_runbook_summary: Pre-upgrade: run preflight, verify artifact signatures and mirror reachability. Online upgrade: use redwoodctl upgrade --mirror <fqdn>. Offline: upload signed artifact via redwoodctl offline-import --file <path>, verify checksums, then apply. During upgrade: monitor metrics and Console timeline; abort on >5% error rate or failing readiness probes. Rollback: redwoodctl rollback --to <previous-version> or automatic rollback if health gate fails. Post-upgrade: validate audit logs and run smoke tests listed in tests.
notes: This document focuses on operator contracts for networking and upgrade safety in constrained environments. Implementation owners should coordinate with Security for credential storage and with Console team for timeline and audit UI changes. Acceptance tests must be runnable in CI with a simulated mirror to avoid dependence on Redwood public infrastructure.
